DIS.rationale: Disney presents a cautiously attractive fundamental picture anchored by a durable franchise moat and a valuation near historical lows, offset by a genuine earnings-quality concern and elevated near-term regulatory risk. The IP-to-parks-to-streaming flywheel is structurally unreplicable: Experiences generated record $10.0B operating income in FY2025 with ~140M annual visitors, and streaming inflected to $1.3B annual profit with SVOD margins crossing 10% for the first time in Q2 FY2026. Operating income has been stable at $4.4B–$4.6B/quarter, cash generation is robust ($6.91B OCF in Q2), and the balance sheet is strengthening (D/E 0.78x, equity up 8% over five quarters). Valuation is compelling: P/E of 14.1x sits at the 5th percentile of its 365-day range (12.5x–23.8x), P/B at 1.507x is at the absolute floor, and the 7.1% earnings yield significantly exceeds the 4.4% 10-year Treasury. However, the central concern is the -29.8% YoY EPS decline on +6.5% revenue growth, indicating below-the-line cost pressure (interest, taxes, non-operating items) that must resolve for the stock to re-rate. The FCC regulatory escalation (broadcast license investigation, $50M carriage settlement) and loss of the Roku platform opportunity to Fox add genuine near-term risk. New CEO D'Amaro's parks-first strategy and the $8B buyback target provide a credible capital-allocation tailwind, and Bank of America's $125 target vs. ~$98 current suggests ~27% upside if earnings stabilize. The score reflects strong franchise quality and cheap valuation tempered by unresolved earnings deterioration and elevated regulatory overhang — modestly positive, not a high-conviction call until the below-the-line pressure clarifies.
